title: Harbor Bridge closes to traffic after inspectors find cracked bearings
excerpt: The city's busiest crossing will stay shut for at least three weeks.
textContent:
The Harbor Bridge, which carries about 90,000 vehicles a day between the port district and the north shore, closed to all traffic at 6 a.m. Tuesday after state inspectors found cracks in two of its steel bearings.

Transportation Secretary Luis Ferreira said the closure would last "at least three weeks" while engineers install temporary supports. "We are not going to take chances with a structure this old," Ferreira told reporters at the bridge's south ramp. "The cracks are small, but they are in the wrong place."

The bridge opened in 1961 and was last fully rehabilitated in 1998. A 2024 state report rated its condition as "fair" and recommended replacing the bearings by 2027.

Commuters were directed to the Eastside Tunnel, where traffic backed up for nearly two miles during the morning rush. The regional transit authority said it would add 40 ferry trips a day starting Wednesday and suspend fares on the Route 12 bus, which runs parallel to the bridge.

Port officials said freight trucks would be routed through the tunnel overnight to ease daytime congestion. Mayor Grace Lindqvist urged residents to work from home where they can.

The state legislature is scheduled to vote next month on a $1.2 billion plan to replace the bridge entirely by 2032.
